title: Staff-tabled 2024–2026 budget and Conestogo Road housing approval
subtitle: Utility rates, reserve changes, licensing fees, student residence rezoning, early capital approvals, Uptown grants and bike summit sponsorship.
overview: Council received the staff-tabled 2024–2026 budget, which proposes property tax increases of 7.46% for 2024, 7.30% for 2025 and 6.44% for 2026. Final adoption is scheduled for February 12, 2024. Staff also tabled a menu of optional reductions and additions that is not included in those figures, and public engagement opportunities run through January.

Council set 2024 utility rates, approved a 12% increase to Building Standards fees, and approved a 4% rental housing rate increase and a 5% business licensing rate increase. It also adopted a new comprehensive business licensing by-law. A reserves update redirected funding to climate action and changed how surpluses are shared. Council also approved $5,750,000 for operations and storage expansion and early approval of several 2024 capital projects.

On land use, Council adopted the official plan amendment and approved the rezoning and draft plan for a large mixed-use, purpose-built rental development at 525 and 565 Conestogo Road West, {{vote:m18}}. It approved a zoning change for a new University of Waterloo student residence, with the holding provision to stay in place until rail noise and vibration requirements are confirmed. Council also extended the SOLER initiative and the Uptown grant programs through 2024, and agreed to sponsor the 2024 Ontario Bike Summit.

decisions.detail: Council received the staff-tabled budget, approved the schedule with final adoption on February 12, 2024, and received documents showing proposed tax increases of 7.46% for 2024, 7.30% for 2025 and 6.44% for 2026.

Council approved a 2024 water rate of $2.32/m3, a sanitary rate of $2.81/m3, new monthly stormwater rates by property type, a 2025–2033 forecast in principle, and an end to blended rates on bi-monthly bills that span two years.

Council redirected funds to the Climate Action Reserve Fund, set 25% splits for any tax and investment surpluses, approved one-time transfers from the RIM Park reserve surplus, and deferred the Northdale parkland transfer to February 2024.

decisions.item: Rental housing and business licensing fees
decisions.detail: Council approved a 4% rental housing rate increase and a 5% business licensing increase for 2024, and let the Rental Housing Reserve run a temporary deficit through 2030.
Council adopted Official Plan Amendment 32, approved the zone change and endorsed the draft plan of subdivision, as amended, including a corrected maximum of 5,452 bedrooms.
Council approved the zoning change for 155 and 165 University Avenue West but will not lift the holding provision until the Region and CN Rail confirm noise and vibration requirements are met.
Council approved $5,750,000 for land and facility acquisition and related work, funded from the tax rate, water and sanitary stabilization reserves and the 2024 Material Storage Building project.
Council approved a $25,000 sponsorship of the April 2024 Ontario Bike Summit in Waterloo, funded from the Community Priority and Contingency Reserve.

debate: On the business licensing by-law, one councillor asked whether businesses that might operate like nightclubs had been consulted. Staff said they met owners and the Uptown BIA, shared the draft schedule and heard positive feedback. Another councillor questioned why only lawyers, paralegals and regulated health professionals were exempt from licensing, and asked that other regulated professions be reviewed next round.

On the utility rates, a councillor raised concern that the stabilization reserves were below target, and asked about water-use reduction, flushing education and low uptake of stormwater credits. Staff said the reserve levels will be reviewed for 2025 rates, that better knowledge of the system and leak detection are priorities, and that more public messaging is warranted.

On the Conestogo Road development, councillors asked about the pedestrian bridge over the highway, which the province has not supported, and about the loss of employment land. Staff said employment lands south of the hydro corridor remain protected. The applicant said the development would be purpose-built rental with a meaningful amount of affordable and attainable housing, but no share was fixed. A resident delegate asked for specific affordable unit numbers and for tools to ensure construction goes ahead.

A councillor asked for legal advice about a letter from a lawyer received just before the meeting before voting on Conestogo Road. Council held a short closed session and then carried the motion {{vote:m18}}. Staff said they were satisfied the report addressed the planning items.

On the student residence, councillors asked about parking, trails during construction and streetscape funds. The university said no parking spaces would be lost and a campus parking study is under way. Resident delegates supported more student housing and wanted more ambition on parking and housing.
